slides.text: HE DIED ON A BEACH WITH NO NAME... FOR 74 YEARS
December 1, 1948. Somerton beach, Adelaide, Australia. A well-dressed man is found dead against the sea wall.
No wallet. No ID. Every label had been cut out of his clothes.
Doctors couldn't say how he died. Possibly poison... but they never found one.
Then they found a secret pocket sewn into his trousers. Inside, a tiny scrap of paper with two words: Tamam Shud.
It means 'it is ended.' It was torn from a book of Persian poems, the Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.
When that exact book turned up, it had a code written in the back. Nobody has ever cracked it.
His suitcase turned up at Adelaide Railway Station. Spy? Smuggler? Heartbroken lover? For decades, nobody even knew his name.
In 2022, researchers used DNA to name him: Carl 'Charles' Webb, an engineer from Melbourne. Why he died... is still a mystery.
